name: FANUC Corporation
fiscal_year_note: Fiscal year ends March 31. Company label FY2026 = Apr 2026 to Mar 2027 (some data sites call it FY2027, e.g. 'Q2 2027'). Q2 FY2026 (Jul-Sep 2026) was released Oct 23, 2026 after the Tokyo close; first trading reaction was Oct 26. Q3 (Oct-Dec) results are normally released in late January.
full_year_guidance: FY2026 (Apr 2026-Mar 2027), raised Oct 23, 2026: net sales JPY 1,013.7bn (+18.2% YoY; prior JPY 948.1bn from Jul 31; initial JPY 909.6bn from Apr 24), operating income JPY 240.7bn (23.7% margin; prior 218.0, initial 212.2), ordinary income JPY 308.8bn, net income JPY 228.3bn (prior 198.0), EPS JPY 246.01. First year above JPY 1tn sales. FX assumption for Oct 2026-Mar 2027: JPY 150/USD and JPY 175/EUR (implied full year JPY 154.69/USD, 179.68/EUR; H1 actual 159.37/USD, 184.35/EUR). Implied H2: sales JPY 540.0bn, OP JPY 124.0bn (23.0% margin) vs 26.0% in Q2 (derived). Interim DPS JPY 72.54 (+41%); year-end DPS not yet set (60% payout ratio in FY2025).
fx_sensitivity: Not disclosed by Fanuc (none in the FY2025, Q1 or Q2 FY2026 materials reviewed). Exposure is high: about 87% of sales are outside Japan (Japan 12.5% of H1 FY2026 sales). Rough estimate, ours and low confidence: about JPY 1.5bn annual OP per JPY 1 move vs USD, about JPY 0.8bn per JPY 1 vs EUR, and roughly JPY 6-8bn OP per 1% broad yen move, assuming foreign-currency revenue carries mostly yen costs. H2 guidance uses JPY 150/USD vs spot about 156.9 (Oct 27), so a steady weak yen is upside to guidance.

physical_ai_exposure.description: Robot division (industrial robots and cobots) was 41.0% of H1 FY2026 sales (44.1% of FY2025). FA (CNC/servo) and Robomachine are adjacent automation. Fanuc holds nearly 20% of the global industrial robot market (Nikkei, via TechNews). Physical AI: NVIDIA collaboration announced Dec 1, 2025 (NVIDIA robot simulation framework in Fanuc software; voice-command, safety and part-tracking robots); five Physical AI systems shown at IMTS 2026 with collaborations with NVIDIA and Google in North America; Physical AI CNC and digital twin; open-platform framework for partners. Management says physical AI inquiries are many but most projects are still trials, and some multi-thousand-unit projects have converted to orders.
physical_ai_exposure.optionality_notes: The NVIDIA tie-up lifted the stock up to 9.4% intraday on Dec 2, 2025 (highest since July 2021) and the physical-AI narrative carried it to a record JPY 8,880 in May 2026. Since then it has de-rated (-36.5% from the high to JPY 5,639) even as orders hit records, because robot orders grew far slower (+12.6% in Q2) than FA/CNC orders (+130%). The current order boom is driven more by AI data centers, semiconductors and humanoid-component machining (CNC demand) than by robots themselves.

cost_and_supply_chain_notes: Management cites tight procurement industry-wide: long lead times for semiconductors, electrical/electronic components and mechanical parts; mitigation through alternative components and 2nd/3rd sources. Rising component costs with a time lag in passing them to prices, plus US tariffs, are named as limits on profit growth; the forecast assumes current US tariffs continue (impact not quantified). April 2026 Q&A flagged possible shortages of oil-derived materials (lubricants, thinners, paint) linked to the Middle East. Capacity not at its limit; capex to rise YoY (FY2025 capex only JPY 22.0bn); robot capacity has headroom. General knowledge, not verified this session: production is concentrated in Japan (Yamanashi HQ complex), China robots also come from the Shanghai-FANUC JV, and most Japanese exports to the US face the 15% US tariff agreed in 2025.
competition_notes: In China (about 30% of orders), longer Fanuc lead times led some customers to adopt competitors' products (Q1 FY2026 Q&A); management says share is not simply declining and varies by application. Some Chinese makers sell extremely low-cost CNCs that Fanuc cannot track. Domestic Chinese brands held about 54% of China's 2025 industrial robot market (MIR, cited by Inovance), and Inovance alone held 9.2% in H1 2026. Pricing: Fanuc says it balances price increases with cost reduction given competitors' positions.
key_drivers: Record orders: Q2 FY2026 JPY 306.0bn (+49.0% YoY, +8.5% QoQ), book-to-bill about 1.26; H1 orders JPY 587.9bn (+43%)
FA (CNC) orders JPY 112.2bn (+130% YoY) on AI data center, semiconductor, humanoid-component and aerospace machining demand
China orders JPY 91.2bn (+79.8%) and Asia ex-China JPY 65.3bn (+111.9%) in Q2; Japan +54.3%
Guidance raised twice this year: OP JPY 212.2bn to 218.0bn to 240.7bn; H2 margin guide of 23.0% vs 26.0% achieved in Q2 looks conservative
Weak yen vs H2 assumption of JPY 150/USD (spot about 156.9)
Shareholder returns: new buyback up to JPY 50bn / 10m shares (1.08%), 60% payout; net cash about JPY 787bn (about 15% of market cap)
Physical AI partnerships (NVIDIA, Google) and open platform could lift robot demand over time
key_risks: Order pull-forward: management says part of the order surge reflects customers ordering early because of long lead times and it is unclear whether the level will continue
Robot division lagging: Q2 robot orders +12.6% and robot sales +7.2% YoY
Yen strength: BOJ raised rates to 1.0% (Jun) and 1.25% (Sep 2026); a stronger yen would cut the FX tailwind
Share loss in China to local brands and low-cost CNC makers
Component cost inflation, procurement bottlenecks and US tariffs
Sentiment/valuation: stock fell 14.3% on record Q1 orders (Aug 3) and 5.5% in the Oct 15 AI sell-off; -36.5% from the May 2026 high

notes: Price is the Oct 26, 2026 close. Shares outstanding exclude 57.36m treasury shares (Sep 30, 2026); Yahoo Japan's JPY 5.54tn market cap uses issued shares. USD conversion at JPY 156.91/USD. total_debt set to 0 as an approximation: no borrowings are disclosed and stockanalysis reports none; lease liabilities not separately disclosed. Order and sales amounts by division/region are derived from the company's composition percentages. Geo and segment mixes are H1 FY2026 sales computed by us (FY2025 geo: Americas 27.1, China 26.6, Europe 17.8, Other Asia 14.5, Japan 12.9). FY2025 R&D of JPY 47.8bn comes from an unlabeled reference-material chart (series order suggests R&D 47.8 and D&A 45.0); medium confidence. FCF = operating CF 250.9 less PP&E purchases 21.2. pe_forward uses company EPS forecast JPY 246.01 (Yahoo Japan shows 23.00x); MarketScreener consensus P/E for FY3/27 was 26.4x at JPY 5,823 before the raise. ev_ebitda_forward is ours: EV (market cap less JPY 787bn cash and securities) over MarketScreener consensus EBITDA of JPY 277.5bn set before the Oct 23 raise, so it likely overstates the multiple; MarketScreener showed 16.9x at JPY 5,823. dividend_yield_pct is trailing (JPY 55.76 FY2025 year-end + JPY 72.54 interim); a 60% payout on EPS JPY 246 implies about JPY 148 and roughly 2.6% forward (estimate). The Q2 FY2026 Q&A summary PDF could not be fetched. FX sensitivity figures are our rough estimates.
